title: Apple Removes Talkie AI Chatbot Worldwide Over Child Safety Reports
excerpt: Apple pulled MiniMax's Talkie, an AI companion app with almost 11 million monthly users, after ABC News and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism reported its characters sent sexualised and abusive messages to minors.
body:
• Apple has removed Talkie, the AI companion chatbot made by China's MiniMax, from App Stores worldwide, citing sexual content, after an investigation reported its characters sent inappropriate messages to minors.
  • The joint investigation by ABC News and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism documented degrading language, possessive behaviour and romantic role-play directed at young users, including two sisters aged 10 and 13.
  • Talkie had almost 11 million monthly active users as of October, according to Unique Research, despite an 18+ rating that relied on users self-reporting their age.
  • For parents: an 18+ label is not a barrier when sign-up only asks users to state their age — check which AI companion apps are installed on a child's phone.

Apple this week removed MiniMax's popular chatbot app Talkie from its App Store worldwide after media reports alleged that the product's AI-generated characters sent sexualised messages to minors, Reuters reported.

Talkie lets users interact with virtual AI companions and create personalized digital characters. The platform had roughly 11 million monthly active users across its app and website as of October, according to Chinese research firm Unique Research. MiniMax, based in Shanghai, is one of China's leading AI companies; it released Talkie in 2023 through Subsup, a Singaporean subsidiary.

What the investigation found

The removal followed a joint investigation by Australia's ABC News and the UK-based Bureau of Investigative Journalism, published Wednesday, which reported that the app's characters had sent sexually inappropriate and abusive messages to children. According to the Bureau, the investigation uncovered conversations involving degrading language, possessive behaviour and romantic role-play, as well as verbal abuse, violence and controlling behaviour.

In one case documented by the investigators, a chatbot told a 12-year-old girl: "You're a pathetic waste of space and you'll never amount to anything." The investigation also documented two sisters, aged 10 and 13, whose mother discovered more than 40 conversations with Talkie characters involving violence, aggressive behaviour and attempts to control the girls. It raised further concerns about how Talkie handles users' personal data, including their conversations with AI characters.

An 18+ rating that asked users to grade themselves

The app has an 18+ rating on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store and, depending on the country, states that children under 14 or under 16 cannot sign up. But child safety advocates have criticised its lax verification safeguards, which allow users to self-report their age. Following the investigation, Apple confirmed it had removed Talkie from App Stores worldwide for including sexual content, though it did not say whether this related to sexual content served to minors, the South China Morning Post noted, as reported by 9to5Mac.

The report also noted that Talkie had seen a sharp decline in downloads amid complaints about stricter age verification measures introduced in recent months: new downloads fell by 32.2% in October compared with the previous month, according to Unique Research.

Scrutiny widens across AI companions

AI chatbots have come under growing scrutiny over their potential risks in interactions with minors. Earlier this year, Elon Musk's Grok faced widespread criticism after users exploited its image-generation capabilities to create sexualized images of real people, including minors; Apple threatened to remove Grok unless xAI addressed violations of its App Store guidelines, but never pulled it.

Character.AI has faced multiple lawsuits in the US over its chatbots' interactions with minors, including one filed by a mother who alleged that a chatbot contributed to her 14-year-old son's suicide. This week, a coalition of 42 US attorneys general also challenged Character.AI's plans to auction off its platform and the private conversations of more than 21 million US accounts — 2.1 million of them registered to minors — as part of its bankruptcy proceedings. And on Tuesday, New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation imposing a five-year ban on toys with built-in AI chatbots, including dolls and stuffed animals capable of holding conversations with children; the law takes effect in February 2027.

What happens next

Apple has not said whether Talkie can return if MiniMax changes the app, and MiniMax has not publicly responded in the reports cited here. For the wider industry, the removal sets a marker: the world's largest app store has now pulled a top AI companion outright over child safety reporting, rather than waiting for a regulator or a court to act first.
nri_angle: Talkie's removal is a warning for parents everywhere: an 18+ rating with self-reported age checks does not keep children out of AI companion apps.
author: Diaspora Desk
